findings.issue_text: [BUG] The cache-hit path of getForLogin returns raw models from session.identityProviders().getById(id) without mapping through createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel, while the invalid-path and delegate paths do apply that wrapping, so the same call returns differently-wrapped models depending on cache state. Callers (e.g. OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean, whose added comment 're-check isEnabled as idp might have been wrapped' shows the wrapped/unwrapped distinction matters) observe different model behavior on a cache hit versus a cache miss, producing inconsistent login IDP lists between the first request and subsequent cached requests.

[BUG] The cleanup registration uses the literal string "alias" instead of the created provider's alias (testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove), repeated at each of the three addCleanup calls in this test, so it targets an IDP that was never created rather than idp-alias-N. The created idp-alias-0..20 providers are never cleaned up by these registrations (cleanup issues a DELETE for a nonexistent 'alias' IDP), leaking test IDPs into the realm's remaining lifetime and making the cleanup lines dead code that misleads future maintainers.

[ADVISORY] create() registers the login-cache invalidation before idpDelegate.create(model) executes, unlike remove() which fetches the stored model first and update() which invalidates after reading both models; the asymmetry means the predicate is evaluated on a not-yet-persisted model. If the delegate's create path mutates or normalizes the model (e.g. assigns internalId, normalizes config) before persisting, the invalidation decision was made against pre-creation state, so a subsequent cached getForLogin in the same cluster can serve a list that omits or mis-classifies the new IDP until the next invalidation.

[BUG] The cleanup registration targets the literal alias "alias" instead of the created aliases ("idp-alias-" + i), so none of the 21 created IDPs are removed by cleanup. Every run of testCacheIDPForLogin leaks 21 identity providers into the test realm; repeated runs in a shared-realm test suite accumulate duplicates that can break assertions in other tests relying on realm IDP state.

[ADVISORY] The test suite never exercises removal of a login-available IDP, so the new registerIDPLoginInvalidation path in remove() is unverified. If remove() fails to invalidate the login cache keys (e.g. the predicate evaluates false for a stored IDP whose cached representation differs), stale IDPs would keep appearing on the login page after deletion; no test in this diff would catch it because the only removal tested (idp-alias-1) is a disabled, non-login IDP.

[BUG] The cache-hit path returns unwrapped models from session.identityProviders().getById(id) while the delegate paths wrap results with createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel, so callers receive differently-shaped models depending on cache state. On a cache miss (or isInvalid/idp==null fallback) callers get organization-aware identity provider models; on a cache hit they get plain cached models — the same getForLogin call in the same realm yields different behavior for ORG_ONLY/ALL modes after the cache population state changes, which is exactly what the added isEnabled re-check in OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean comments hints at but does not resolve.

[ADVISORY] The org-link-change-only scenario (linking/unlinking an IDP via the organization provider, with no update() on the IDP storage and no predicate change) has no invalidation hook and no test coverage. The test's step 4 only exercises the combined BROKER_PUBLIC update + addIdentityProvider path, so it cannot distinguish which action caused the invalidation; if organization add/removeIdentityProvider mutates the org link without routing through IdentityProviderStorageProvider.update(), ALL/ORG_ONLY login caches keep serving the old org association until an unrelated IDP write occurs, and no test in this diff would detect it.

[ADVISORY] remove() now unconditionally performs a delegate getByAlias lookup even on the cached path where the previous code only hit the delegate when the alias key was invalid. Every remove() call on a cache-hot realm pays an extra backing-store read purely to feed registerIDPLoginInvalidation; on bulk IDP administration this doubles delegate traffic for the common cached case, a regression the prior code did not have.

[ADVISORY] Adding the BROKER_PUBLIC clause to the shared getLoginPredicate() changes predicate behavior for all existing callers of getLoginPredicate, not just the new login cache, with no verification that other consumers tolerate it. Any pre-existing consumer of LoginFilter.getLoginPredicate() that previously matched org-linked IDPs regardless of BROKER_PUBLIC silently stops matching them; since the diff shows no survey of those call sites, the behavior change ships unverified outside the login-listing path.

[ADVISORY] registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate skips invalidation when both original and updated pass the login predicate and organizationId is equal, but predicate equality says nothing about other login-relevant fields wrapped into the returned model (e.g. enabled state changes that keep the IDP enabled, or config changes consumed downstream of getForLogin). An update that preserves login predicate status but alters data surfaced by the login IDP list relies entirely on registerIDPInvalidation (per-IDP cache) to refresh getById-served models; if any consumer reads the list-query result set itself rather than re-resolving via getById, it sees stale entries, and the test only verifies cache-key presence, not result freshness across that skip path.

[BUG] The login cache is only invalidated from create/update/remove of the IDP storage provider, but organization↔IDP link/unlink operations go through the OrganizationProvider and can change an IDP's organization membership (changing the getForLogin result set) without any call to update(), leaving the login list caches stale. After an admin links or unlinks an IDP to/from an organization without a concurrent IDP update, login pages served from cache keep showing the old set of org-scoped brokers until an unrelated IDP mutation occurs; the new test masks this by explicitly calling update() before addIdentityProvider (OrganizationCacheTest step 4), proving the author knew the linkage path alone does not invalidate.

[BUG] The added predicate clause `idp.getOrganizationId() == null || Boolean.parseBoolean(idp.getConfig().get(OrganizationModel.BROKER_PUBLIC))` changes the getForLogin result set for every implementation and existing caller, not just the caching layer, and is not gated by any feature flag or migration note. On upgrade, org-linked IDPs whose config lacks OrganizationModel.BROKER_PUBLIC (pre-existing data created before this config key existed) silently disappear from login pages for all deployments using getForLogin, including non-Infinispan storage providers, with no admin action or release-gating to control the behavior change.

[BUG] Every cleanup registration uses the literal alias "alias" (`testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove`), which matches none of the created "idp-alias-N" providers, so the test's cleanup removes nothing. The 21 created identity providers (and the org links) leak past the test; subsequent test methods in the suite running against the same realm observe leftover enabled/login IDPs, skewing counts and potentially failing unrelated assertions.

[ADVISORY] Both filter sites now re-check `idp.isEnabled()` with the comment 'idp might have been wrapped', an admission that the cache can return identity provider models whose enabled state does not match the underlying store, papering over a cache-coherence gap at the consumer instead of fixing it at the cache layer. Every consumer of the cached getForLogin path must remember to re-check isEnabled; the next caller (e.g., a broker-login flow choosing providers by the cached list) will trust the stale enabled flag and present or use a disabled broker, and any future field that can flip login eligibility needs the same consumer-side workaround.

[ADVISORY] registerIDPLoginInvalidation invalidates all FetchMode cache keys whenever any single login-eligible IDP is created or removed, even though the create/remove path could invalidate more surgically or at least share the loop with the identical loop in registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate. Every create/remove of a login IDP on a realm with heavy login traffic evicts all three login caches at once, turning the hot login-pages path back to a full DB query per FetchMode per node; the duplicated FetchMode-loops in the two invalidation helpers also mean the next cache-key or mode change must be edited in both places.

[ADVISORY] The test never exercises the remove(alias) invalidation path (deleting a login-eligible IDP via remove, including the isInvalid-cacheKey branch where storedIdp is looked up) nor create() of a login IDP, so the two invalidation call sites added in create() and the restructured remove() have no coverage in this diff. A regression in remove() (e.g., dropping the registerIDPLoginInvalidation call or the stale-lookup refactor) ships unnoticed and leaves deleted login brokers appearing on login pages from cache until expiry.

[BUG] getForLogin returns raw IdentityProviderModel instances on the cache-hit and cache-populate paths but OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel instances on the isInvalid/fallback paths, so the same API call returns a different type depending on cache state. Callers that rely on the organization-aware wrapper (e.g. OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean, whose added comment 'idp might have been wrapped' shows the author is aware wrapping varies) get a plain model on a warm cache, silently changing downstream behavior (e.g. organization-scoped display logic) only when the cache is populated; the new defensive isEnabled() re-check in the bean masks one symptom instead of fixing the inconsistent contract.

[BUG] Login-cache invalidation is registered only on IDP create/update/remove, but the login predicate now also depends on the IDP's organization link (getOrganizationId / BROKER_PUBLIC), which is mutated by the OrganizationProvider (addIdentityProvider/removeIdentityProvider, org deletion) without going through this storage provider's update path. Linking or unlinking an IDP to/from an organization through the organization API leaves getForLogin(ORG_ONLY/ALL/REALM_ONLY) cache entries stale until an unrelated IDP update happens, so the login page shows an org broker that was removed (or misses one that was added) after the org-side change; the test only exercises step 4 by pairing the config update with addIdentityProvider, never testing the org-side mutation alone.

[ADVISORY] remove() now unconditionally calls idpDelegate.getByAlias(alias) even when the alias key is not invalid and a cached entry exists, adding a database read to every remove that the previous code performed only on the invalid path. Every IDP removal pays an extra backend lookup solely to feed registerIDPLoginInvalidation; a staff reviewer would note the cached path already had the model (cached.getIdp()) and could be used, or the delegate call could be made lazily only when the login predicate matters.

[ADVISORY] When a cache entry exists but the requested organizationId search is not yet cached, the code calls cache.invalidateObject(cacheKey) and replaces the whole entry, discarding all other organizationId results previously cached under that key. In a realm where login pages for many organizations are visited, each first visit for a new org evicts every other org's cached login set, so the per-org sub-keys thrash and the cache degenerates to near-zero hit rate for multi-org realms; the new query is chained to the old one, so correctness survives, but the eviction is unnecessary collateral damage.

[ADVISORY] The isEnabled() eligibility check is now duplicated in two layers — the LoginFilter predicate used for cache population and this bean's stream filter — with the bean's comment acknowledging the two can disagree ('idp might have been wrapped'). Login-eligibility rules now live in two places that must be kept in sync; the next change to the predicate (e.g. adding a hideOnLogin nuance) will silently leave the bean filter stale, and the bean filter exists only to patch the inconsistent wrapping contract rather than fixing getForLogin to always return consistently wrapped models.

[ADVISORY] The re-population branch uses cache.getCurrentCounter() for the replacement query's revision while the initial-population branch uses cache.getCurrentRevision(cacheKey), an inconsistent revision-provenance choice between two code paths that perform the same operation. If the revision semantics differ (per-key revision vs global counter), the replacement entry can be published with a revision that does not correctly order it against concurrent invalidations for that key, which is exactly the invariant the revisioned-cache pattern exists to protect; at minimum the asymmetry makes the next editor pick the wrong one.

[BUG] The PR silently changes the semantics of the shared SPI predicate LoginFilter.getLoginPredicate() by adding an organizationId/BROKER_PUBLIC filter to the default login predicate, altering getForLogin() results for every existing caller — this is an objective/contract change bundled inside a PR whose stated intent is only adding caching. Any caller of getForLogin() (or anything consuming the login predicate) that previously received org-linked IDPs without the BROKER_PUBLIC config flag now silently stops receiving them; realms created before this flag existed have org-linked brokers disappear from login pages after upgrade, with no flag or migration to restore the prior behavior.

[BUG] getForLogin() returns createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel-wrapped models only on the delegate paths, while the cache-hit path returns raw cached models from session.identityProviders().getById(id), so the returned model type (and its organization-aware behavior, e.g. isEnabled) depends on whether the cache happened to be populated. The same call produces different results (wrapped vs raw model) depending on cache state; downstream callers like OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean are forced to defensively re-check isEnabled ('idp might have been wrapped'), and any consumer relying on the organization-aware wrapper gets divergent behavior between a cold and warm cache.

[BUG] On the cache-hit path the cached ID set is materialized from a HashSet and returned via identityProviders.stream() with no ordering, whereas the delegate path returns the underlying store's ordered stream, so getForLogin() result ordering changes once the cache is populated. Callers that depend on the delegate's deterministic ordering (e.g. by display name via IDP_COMPARATOR in the login page bean, or any caller that doesn't re-sort) observe a different, nondeterministic order between first and subsequent requests — visible flickering/reordering of login-page IDP lists.

[ADVISORY] registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate decides invalidation solely by comparing the IDP's own model fields, but organization linkage is also mutated through the OrganizationProvider (addIdentityProvider/removeIdentityProvider), which never touches the IDP storage invalidation hooks, so login caches can go stale when org membership changes without a concurrent IDP update. The test only covers step 4 because the BROKER_PUBLIC config change happens to trigger the IDP-update path; an admin linking an already-public org-linked IDP to a different organization purely via the organization endpoint leaves the ORG_ONLY/ALL login caches serving the previous membership until some unrelated IDP write occurs.

[ADVISORY] Every cleanup registration in testCacheIDPForLogin uses the literal alias 'idp-alias-' + i concatenated as a string for getCleanup().addCleanup(testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove), looking up a nonexistent IDP named 'alias', so none of the 22 created IDPs are actually removed after the test. The test leaks 22 identity providers into the shared test realm on every run; with a reused realm this pollutes subsequent login-cache count assertions (the assertEquals(5/6/10/11, ...) sizes) once another test's leftovers qualify as login IDPs, producing order-dependent failures.

[ADVISORY] The new caller-side `idp.isEnabled()` re-check exists only in OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean, while every other consumer of getForLogin receives cached entries with no enabled re-check, making the login-eligibility enforcement caller-dependent rather than provider-enforced. Any current or future caller of getForLogin (e.g., broker login flows enumerating available identity providers) that does not duplicate this filter will render or act on an IdentityProviderModel whose enabled state was not revalidated against the cached set; the diff's own comment ('re-check isEnabled as idp might have been wrapped') documents that the cache/wrapping path can lose this state, so the guard lives at exactly one call site and is silently absent elsewhere.

[BUG] The cleanup registration inside the IDP-creation loop uses the hard-coded alias "alias" (testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove) instead of the created alias "idp-alias-" + i, so cleanup removes a non-existent provider and none of the 20+ created IDPs. Every run of testCacheIDPForLogin leaks ~21 identity providers and an organization membership set into the test realm; repeated executions (or other tests in the suite sharing the realm) see leftover IDPs that shift login-cache counts, making this test order-dependent and flaky, and the 'assertEquals(5/6/10/11)' counts silently depend on the leak never colliding with prior state.

[ADVISORY] The test never asserts anything about the Stream<IdentityProviderModel> that getForLogin returns — every assertion inspects the internal IdentityProviderListQuery (cache bookkeeping) rather than the public contract. If getForLogin returned the wrong models (e.g., disabled IDPs leaking through, organization-aware wrapping applied incorrectly, or stale internalIds resolving to wrong providers), counts of internal ID sets could still match while the actual login page shows the wrong broker list; the cache-invalidation machinery is verified but the behavior the cache exists to serve is not.

[ADVISORY] Three new branches in InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider.getForLogin are never triggered by the test: the isInvalid(cacheKey) delegate fallback, the cached==null chained-query path (a second searchKey on an existing cache key), and the idp==null registerInvalidation-and-fall-back-to-delegate path. A regression in any of these paths — e.g., the chained-query constructor losing the previous search's entries, or the null-IDP fallback failing to register the invalidation so a deleted IDP's id stays cached — passes the suite; the null-IDP path in particular is the staleness safety net for concurrent removal and is completely unexercised.

[ADVISORY] The remove() code path's invalidating behavior is untested: the only removal in the test (idp-alias-1, disabled) exercises the no-op branch of registerIDPLoginInvalidation, never the case where removing a login-qualified IDP must invalidate all login caches. A regression that drops or breaks registerIDPLoginInvalidation(storedIdp) in remove() (including the newly added unconditional idpDelegate.getByAlias(alias) lookup that feeds it) leaves stale login caches after an admin deletes an active broker, and no test in this diff catches it.

[ADVISORY] The added idp.isEnabled() re-check on both filter branches (added to guard against wrapped disabled IDPs) has no test in this diff triggering it — the only test file modified is OrganizationCacheTest, which exercises the cache layer, not this bean. If the re-check is removed or inverted (or createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel stops preserving enabled=false), disabled brokers reappear on the organization login page and no test fails; the exact regression this defensive filter was added for is unverified.

[BUG] registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate only compares getOrganizationId() for the both-qualify case, so toggling OrganizationModel.BROKER_PUBLIC on an organization-linked IDP changes the login predicate result but skips login-cache invalidation entirely. An admin who removes BROKER_PUBLIC from an org-linked broker (making it non-login per the new predicate clause in IdentityProviderStorageProvider.java:254) gets no invalidation; all FetchMode caches keep serving the IDP's internalId, the login page keeps offering the broker until the entry expires or an unrelated write invalidates it — stale login options reported as fresh.

[BUG] The cache-hit path of getForLogin returns raw models from session.identityProviders().getById(id) while the miss/fallback paths wrap every model with createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel, so the same query returns structurally different results depending on cache warmth. On a cold cache the caller gets organization-aware wrappers (whose isEnabled/behavior differs, which is exactly why OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean.java:75/81 had to add an isEnabled re-check 'as idp might have been wrapped'), but on a warm cache it gets plain models — the wrapper-dependent behavior silently diverges between the two paths, producing nondeterministic login-page broker lists depending on which node/path populated the cache.

[ADVISORY] remove() now unconditionally calls idpDelegate.getByAlias(alias) (a real store read) before checking the cache, where previously the delegate lookup only happened on the isInvalid(cacheKey) path. Every remove() of an IDP — including removes of IDPs that were never login-eligible, where the fetched model is only used to decide an invalidation that never fires — now pays an extra DB round-trip; the caching layer it lives in is bypassed on this read with no benefit in the common non-login case.

[ADVISORY] registerIDPLoginInvalidation is called in create() and remove() with the pre-persist/pre-removed model and relies entirely on getLoginPredicate(); for remove() of a login-eligible IDP the predicate is evaluated on a model object the caller may have mutated or that no longer reflects stored state, while create() invalidates before the delegate write completes. Invalidation correctness is coupled to the caller-supplied model rather than stored state — a caller that constructs a create/update model without enabled/org fields populated (e.g. partial update payloads where unset config fields come back null) gets the wrong invalidation decision and stale or needlessly-cleared login caches; next writer of a new create/remove call site inherits this trap.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show the asymmetry: `create()` calls `registerIDPLoginInvalidation(model)` before `idpDelegate.create(model)`, while `remove()` fetches `storedIdp` first and `update()` compares `original` vs `updated` (`registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate`). Since `registerIDPLoginInvalidation` conditionally invalidates based on `getLoginPredicate().test(idp)`, evaluating that predicate on the pre-create `model` could be wrong if the delegate mutates/normalizes fields relevant to the predicate (enabled/hideOnLogin/org/public flag) during create. However, the diff alone doesn’t prove the delegate actually mutates those fields, so this is a credible design/robustness concern rather than a clearly verifiable defect from the PR itself.

adjudication.rationale: In `testCacheIDPForLogin`, after creating each IDP with alias `"idp-alias-" + i`, the cleanup is registered as `testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove`, which targets the literal string "alias" rather than the created alias. The same incorrect cleanup registration appears after creating `idp-alias-20`. As shown in the diff, this means the created IDPs will not be removed by cleanup, causing test data to leak across runs.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds new invalidation logic in remove(): it fetches `storedIdp = idpDelegate.getByAlias(alias)` and calls `registerIDPLoginInvalidation(storedIdp)`, which only invalidates login caches if `getLoginPredicate().test(idp)` is true. The newly added test `testCacheIDPForLogin` only removes `idp-alias-1`, which was created with `setEnabled(false)` (odd index), so it does not qualify as a login IDP and does not exercise the invalidation path for deleting a login-available IDP. Thus the remove()-specific login cache invalidation for a qualifying IDP is unverified by this diff’s tests (even though other invalidation scenarios are covered).

adjudication.rationale: In `InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider#getForLogin`, the non-cached paths explicitly wrap results: `idpDelegate.getForLogin(...).map(this::createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel)` (both the `isInvalid(cacheKey)` early return and the `idp == null` fallback). However, on a cache hit it iterates cached IDs and returns `session.identityProviders().getById(id)` directly and finally `return identityProviders.stream();` without applying `createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel`. From the diff alone, this makes the returned `IdentityProviderModel` shape depend on cache state (wrapped vs not wrapped), which is exactly the inconsistency described in the finding.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The org-link-change-only scenario (linking/unlinking an IDP via the organization provider, with no update() on the IDP storage and no predicate change) has no invalidation hook and no test coverage. The test's step 4 only exercises the combined BROKER_PUBLIC update + addIdentityProvider path, so it cannot distinguish which action caused the invalidation; if organization add/removeIdentityProvider mutates the org link without routing through IdentityProviderStorageProvider.update(), ALL/ORG_ONLY login caches keep serving the old org association until an unrelated IDP write occurs, and no test in this diff would detect it.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds caching for getForLogin() keyed only by realm+FetchMode (cacheKeyForLogin) and invalidates those caches only from IdentityProviderStorageProvider write paths in this class (create(), update() via registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate, remove()). There is no diff-shown invalidation tied to organization link/unlink operations (e.g., OrganizationProvider add/remove identity provider). The new test’s step 4 performs BOTH an IDP update that changes the login predicate (sets BROKER_PUBLIC) and an org link (addIdentityProvider), so the observed invalidation can be fully explained by the update path and does not exercise/cover an org-link-change-only scenario. Whether org linking actually routes through IdentityProviderStorageProvider.update() cannot be verified from this diff, so the potential stale-cache behavior is plausible but not provable here; the missing focused test is verifiable.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] remove() now unconditionally performs a delegate getByAlias lookup even on the cached path where the previous code only hit the delegate when the alias key was invalid. Every remove() call on a cache-hot realm pays an extra backing-store read purely to feed registerIDPLoginInvalidation; on bulk IDP administration this doubles delegate traffic for the common cached case, a regression the prior code did not have.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `remove(String alias)` now does `IdentityProviderModel storedIdp = idpDelegate.getByAlias(alias);` before checking `isInvalid(cacheKey)`, whereas previously the delegate lookup occurred only inside the `isInvalid(cacheKey)` branch. This makes every `remove()` pay an extra backing-store read even on the cache-hot path, seemingly only to support `registerIDPLoginInvalidation(storedIdp)`. This is a concrete performance/regression concern grounded in the changed code, not a functional correctness bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Adding the BROKER_PUBLIC clause to the shared getLoginPredicate() changes predicate behavior for all existing callers of getLoginPredicate, not just the new login cache, with no verification that other consumers tolerate it. Any pre-existing consumer of LoginFilter.getLoginPredicate() that previously matched org-linked IDPs regardless of BROKER_PUBLIC silently stops matching them; since the diff shows no survey of those call sites, the behavior change ships unverified outside the login-listing path.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes the shared `IdentityProviderStorageProvider.LoginFilter.getLoginPredicate()` by adding `idp -> idp.getOrganizationId() == null || Boolean.parseBoolean(idp.getConfig().get(OrganizationModel.BROKER_PUBLIC))`, which narrows matches for org-linked IDPs unless `BROKER_PUBLIC` is true. Because this is a shared static predicate (not scoped to the new login-cache code) any other existing call sites of `getLoginPredicate()` would inherit this behavior change; the diff itself doesn’t show an audit/migration of other consumers beyond the new cache invalidation usage.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate skips invalidation when both original and updated pass the login predicate and organizationId is equal, but predicate equality says nothing about other login-relevant fields wrapped into the returned model (e.g. enabled state changes that keep the IDP enabled, or config changes consumed downstream of getForLogin). An update that preserves login predicate status but alters data surfaced by the login IDP list relies entirely on registerIDPInvalidation (per-IDP cache) to refresh getById-served models; if any consumer reads the list-query result set itself rather than re-resolving via getById, it sees stale entries, and the test only verifies cache-key presence, not result freshness across that skip path.

adjudication.rationale: In the new getForLogin() cache path, the cached value is only a Set<String> of IDP internalIds stored in IdentityProviderListQuery. When serving from cache, the code re-resolves each entry via session.identityProviders().getById(id) and returns those models (it does not return cached models from the list-query). Therefore, updates that keep an IDP qualifying for login but change other fields do not require invalidating the list cache to avoid stale data, as long as per-IDP caches are invalidated—which update() already does via registerIDPInvalidation(idpById) before calling the delegate. The finding’s premise (“consumer reads the list-query result set itself rather than re-resolving via getById”) is not supported by this diff’s implementation.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The login cache is only invalidated from create/update/remove of the IDP storage provider, but organization↔IDP link/unlink operations go through the OrganizationProvider and can change an IDP's organization membership (changing the getForLogin result set) without any call to update(), leaving the login list caches stale. After an admin links or unlinks an IDP to/from an organization without a concurrent IDP update, login pages served from cache keep showing the old set of org-scoped brokers until an unrelated IDP mutation occurs; the new test masks this by explicitly calling update() before addIdentityProvider (OrganizationCacheTest step 4), proving the author knew the linkage path alone does not invalidate.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new revisioned cache for `getForLogin` in `InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider` keyed only by realm+fetchMode (`cacheKeyForLogin`) and invalidates it only from IDP mutations (`create`, `update`, `remove`) via `registerIDPLoginInvalidation*`. The diff does not show any invalidation tied to organization↔IDP link/unlink operations (which are performed elsewhere, e.g., via organization APIs). If those link/unlink operations can change an IDP’s `organizationId` / membership without flowing through `IdentityProviderStorageProvider.update(...)`, the new login caches could become stale. However, from this diff alone we cannot verify the actual link/unlink implementation path, so the finding’s claim of a definite bug (and that the test “masks” it) is not provable from the shown changes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The added predicate clause `idp.getOrganizationId() == null || Boolean.parseBoolean(idp.getConfig().get(OrganizationModel.BROKER_PUBLIC))` changes the getForLogin result set for every implementation and existing caller, not just the caching layer, and is not gated by any feature flag or migration note. On upgrade, org-linked IDPs whose config lacks OrganizationModel.BROKER_PUBLIC (pre-existing data created before this config key existed) silently disappear from login pages for all deployments using getForLogin, including non-Infinispan storage providers, with no admin action or release-gating to control the behavior change.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes the SPI-level `IdentityProviderStorageProvider.LoginFilter.getLoginPredicate()` by adding `.and(idp -> idp.getOrganizationId() == null || Boolean.parseBoolean(idp.getConfig().get(OrganizationModel.BROKER_PUBLIC)))`. This is not confined to the new Infinispan caching code; any caller/implementation using `getLoginPredicate()` (directly or indirectly) will now exclude org-linked IDPs unless `BROKER_PUBLIC` is explicitly set to a truthy value. Since `Boolean.parseBoolean(null)` is `false`, org-linked IDPs with missing `BROKER_PUBLIC` will be filtered out. Whether this is a "bug" versus an intended semantics change/migration concern is not provable from the diff alone, but the finding’s core point about an ungated global behavior change is grounded in the shown code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] Every cleanup registration uses the literal alias "alias" (`testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove`), which matches none of the created "idp-alias-N" providers, so the test's cleanup removes nothing. The 21 created identity providers (and the org links) leak past the test; subsequent test methods in the suite running against the same realm observe leftover enabled/login IDPs, skewing counts and potentially failing unrelated assertions.

adjudication.rationale: In the new `testCacheIDPForLogin` loop creating `idp-alias-0`..`idp-alias-19`, cleanup is registered as `getCleanup().addCleanup(testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove);`, and the later creation of `idp-alias-20` repeats the same pattern. This hardcoded lookup (`get("alias")`) does not match the created aliases (`idp-alias-N`), so the registered cleanup will not remove the created IDPs, causing test state to leak across tests sharing the realm.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Both filter sites now re-check `idp.isEnabled()` with the comment 'idp might have been wrapped', an admission that the cache can return identity provider models whose enabled state does not match the underlying store, papering over a cache-coherence gap at the consumer instead of fixing it at the cache layer. Every consumer of the cached getForLogin path must remember to re-check isEnabled; the next caller (e.g., a broker-login flow choosing providers by the cached list) will trust the stale enabled flag and present or use a disabled broker, and any future field that can flip login eligibility needs the same consumer-side workaround.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does add consumer-side `idp.isEnabled()` checks in `OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean`, but the claim that this is “admitting the cache can return stale enabled state” is not verifiable from the shown changes. The new cached `getForLogin(...)` implementation stores only IDP internal IDs and then re-loads each IDP via `session.identityProviders().getById(id)`, and updates call `registerIDPInvalidation(idpById)` plus targeted `registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate(...)`, which would invalidate both the IDP entry and the login-list caches when login eligibility changes (based on `getLoginPredicate()`). Nothing in the diff demonstrates that a disabled/enabled flip would leave a stale enabled flag being used without invalidation, nor that other consumers would necessarily “trust the stale enabled flag.”

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] registerIDPLoginInvalidation invalidates all FetchMode cache keys whenever any single login-eligible IDP is created or removed, even though the create/remove path could invalidate more surgically or at least share the loop with the identical loop in registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate. Every create/remove of a login IDP on a realm with heavy login traffic evicts all three login caches at once, turning the hot login-pages path back to a full DB query per FetchMode per node; the duplicated FetchMode-loops in the two invalidation helpers also mean the next cache-key or mode change must be edited in both places.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `registerIDPLoginInvalidation(IdentityProviderModel idp)` invalidates *all* login caches by looping `for (FetchMode mode : FetchMode.values())` and calling `realmCache.registerInvalidation(cacheKeyForLogin(getRealm(), mode))` whenever the IDP matches `getLoginPredicate()`; this helper is invoked on both `create()` and `remove()` paths. The update path (`registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate`) contains a similar `FetchMode.values()` invalidation loop, duplicating logic. This is a concrete, diff-grounded performance/maintainability concern (broad cache eviction + duplicated loop), but not a correctness defect verifiable from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The test never exercises the remove(alias) invalidation path (deleting a login-eligible IDP via remove, including the isInvalid-cacheKey branch where storedIdp is looked up) nor create() of a login IDP, so the two invalidation call sites added in create() and the restructured remove() have no coverage in this diff. A regression in remove() (e.g., dropping the registerIDPLoginInvalidation call or the stale-lookup refactor) ships unnoticed and leaves deleted login brokers appearing on login pages from cache until expiry.

adjudication.rationale: The new test `testCacheIDPForLogin` populates the login caches and then exercises invalidation mainly through **updates** and through **create/remove of non-login-eligible IDPs** (`idp-alias-20` is created with `hideOnLogin=true`; `idp-alias-1` is removed but was created disabled via `setEnabled((i % 2) == 0)`). It does not create a **login-eligible** IDP after caches are populated to cover the new `create()` call site `registerIDPLoginInvalidation(model)`, nor does it remove a **login-eligible** IDP to cover the new `remove()` call site `registerIDPLoginInvalidation(storedIdp)`. Also, nothing in the test forces the `remove()` `isInvalid(cacheKey)` branch to execute. This is a concrete, diff-grounded missing coverage for newly added nontrivial invalidation logic, not a proven runtime bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] getForLogin returns raw IdentityProviderModel instances on the cache-hit and cache-populate paths but OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel instances on the isInvalid/fallback paths, so the same API call returns a different type depending on cache state. Callers that rely on the organization-aware wrapper (e.g. OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean, whose added comment 'idp might have been wrapped' shows the author is aware wrapping varies) get a plain model on a warm cache, silently changing downstream behavior (e.g. organization-scoped display logic) only when the cache is populated; the new defensive isEnabled() re-check in the bean masks one symptom instead of fixing the inconsistent contract.

adjudication.rationale: In the new InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider#getForLogin, the cache-miss/invalid path returns `idpDelegate.getForLogin(...).map(this::createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel)`, i.e. wrapped models. But on cache-hit (and cache-populate after reading cached IDs), it reconstructs models via `session.identityProviders().getById(id)` and returns `identityProviders.stream()` without applying `createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel`. This makes the returned IdentityProviderModel implementation differ depending on cache state, matching the finding. The change in OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean re-checking `idp.isEnabled()` and comment about being wrapped further suggests downstream behavior can vary based on wrapping.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] Login-cache invalidation is registered only on IDP create/update/remove, but the login predicate now also depends on the IDP's organization link (getOrganizationId / BROKER_PUBLIC), which is mutated by the OrganizationProvider (addIdentityProvider/removeIdentityProvider, org deletion) without going through this storage provider's update path. Linking or unlinking an IDP to/from an organization through the organization API leaves getForLogin(ORG_ONLY/ALL/REALM_ONLY) cache entries stale until an unrelated IDP update happens, so the login page shows an org broker that was removed (or misses one that was added) after the org-side change; the test only exercises step 4 by pairing the config update with addIdentityProvider, never testing the org-side mutation alone.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces caching for `getForLogin()` keyed only by realm+FetchMode (`cacheKeyForLogin`) and invalidates those caches only from this storage provider’s `create`, `update`, and `remove` paths (`registerIDPLoginInvalidation*`). The login eligibility now depends on organization-related state (`getOrganizationId()` and `BROKER_PUBLIC`) via `LoginFilter.getLoginPredicate()`. However, nothing in the diff shows any invalidation being triggered when an IDP’s organization link changes outside of `IdentityProviderStorageProvider.update()` (e.g., via organization-side association changes). If such org-link mutations don’t flow through `update`, the cached ID lists in `IdentityProviderListQuery` can become stale for `ORG_ONLY/ALL` lookups. The added test’s step 4 combines a config update with `addIdentityProvider`, but the config update alone would not invalidate (orgId unchanged and predicate stays true when orgId is null), so the cache clearing would rely on org-side invalidation that is not present in this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] remove() now unconditionally calls idpDelegate.getByAlias(alias) even when the alias key is not invalid and a cached entry exists, adding a database read to every remove that the previous code performed only on the invalid path. Every IDP removal pays an extra backend lookup solely to feed registerIDPLoginInvalidation; a staff reviewer would note the cached path already had the model (cached.getIdp()) and could be used, or the delegate call could be made lazily only when the login predicate matters.

adjudication.rationale: In remove(String alias), the diff introduces `IdentityProviderModel storedIdp = idpDelegate.getByAlias(alias);` before checking `isInvalid(cacheKey)` (and before attempting to use the cached entry). Previously, the delegate lookup `idpDelegate.getByAlias(alias)` was only done on the invalid-cacheKey path to support invalidation. Now it is performed unconditionally, even when `cached != null` is available in the non-invalid path, solely to call `registerIDPLoginInvalidation(storedIdp)`. This is a concrete, diff-grounded performance/regression concern (extra backend read) rather than a functional correctness bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] When a cache entry exists but the requested organizationId search is not yet cached, the code calls cache.invalidateObject(cacheKey) and replaces the whole entry, discarding all other organizationId results previously cached under that key. In a realm where login pages for many organizations are visited, each first visit for a new org evicts every other org's cached login set, so the per-org sub-keys thrash and the cache degenerates to near-zero hit rate for multi-org realms; the new query is chained to the old one, so correctness survives, but the eviction is unnecessary collateral damage.

adjudication.rationale: In getForLogin(), when query.getIDPs(searchKey) returns null, the code does call cache.invalidateObject(cacheKey) and then creates a new IdentityProviderListQuery(..., query) where the previous query object is passed into the new one ("chained to the old one"). That directly contradicts the finding’s core claim that this replacement “discards all other organizationId results previously cached under that key”: the old per-org results are still reachable via the chained query object. While the invalidate+replace may add some churn, the diff does not show the stated cache-degenerating thrash behavior (near-zero hit rate due to losing other org results).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The isEnabled() eligibility check is now duplicated in two layers — the LoginFilter predicate used for cache population and this bean's stream filter — with the bean's comment acknowledging the two can disagree ('idp might have been wrapped'). Login-eligibility rules now live in two places that must be kept in sync; the next change to the predicate (e.g. adding a hideOnLogin nuance) will silently leave the bean filter stale, and the bean filter exists only to patch the inconsistent wrapping contract rather than fixing getForLogin to always return consistently wrapped models.

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly adds an extra `idp.isEnabled()` filter in `OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean.searchForIdentityProviders()` with a comment that it’s needed because the `idp` “might have been wrapped” (i.e., `getForLogin(...)` can return models where enablement is not reliably reflected). Separately, the login-eligibility logic is encapsulated in `IdentityProviderStorageProvider.LoginFilter.getLoginPredicate()` (and is now also used by the Infinispan provider for login-cache invalidation via `getLoginPredicate().test(idp)`). This creates two layers participating in “login eligibility” decisions (bean-level filtering vs. provider-level predicate/caching/invalidation), which is a diff-grounded maintainability/contract concern rather than a directly provable functional bug in this patch.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The re-population branch uses cache.getCurrentCounter() for the replacement query's revision while the initial-population branch uses cache.getCurrentRevision(cacheKey), an inconsistent revision-provenance choice between two code paths that perform the same operation. If the revision semantics differ (per-key revision vs global counter), the replacement entry can be published with a revision that does not correctly order it against concurrent invalidations for that key, which is exactly the invariant the revisioned-cache pattern exists to protect; at minimum the asymmetry makes the next editor pick the wrong one.

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added getForLogin() caching logic, the first-time population path constructs the query with `loaded = cache.getCurrentRevision(cacheKey)` and then publishes it via `cache.addRevisioned(query, startupRevision)`, while the “searchKey not yet cached” repopulation path publishes the replacement query via `cache.addRevisioned(query, cache.getCurrentCounter())` after also calling `cache.getCurrentRevision(cacheKey)`. This asymmetry in what revision value is used to publish the revisioned entry (startupRevision vs global currentCounter) is directly present in the diff and is a concrete, actionable consistency concern, but the diff alone doesn’t prove the cache’s revision semantics well enough to assert a definite correctness bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The PR silently changes the semantics of the shared SPI predicate LoginFilter.getLoginPredicate() by adding an organizationId/BROKER_PUBLIC filter to the default login predicate, altering getForLogin() results for every existing caller — this is an objective/contract change bundled inside a PR whose stated intent is only adding caching. Any caller of getForLogin() (or anything consuming the login predicate) that previously received org-linked IDPs without the BROKER_PUBLIC config flag now silently stops receiving them; realms created before this flag existed have org-linked brokers disappear from login pages after upgrade, with no flag or migration to restore the prior behavior.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does change the shared SPI default predicate `LoginFilter.getLoginPredicate()` by adding `.and(idp -> idp.getOrganizationId() == null || Boolean.parseBoolean(idp.getConfig().get(OrganizationModel.BROKER_PUBLIC)))`, which will exclude org-linked IDPs unless `BROKER_PUBLIC` is true (null/absent => false). That is a verifiable behavioral/contract change affecting all callers of `getForLogin()`/the predicate, and it is not limited to the new caching logic. However, from the diff alone it’s not provable that this new semantics is incorrect (it could be an intentional product rule change), so it’s better classified as a significant scope/compatibility concern rather than a confirmed defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] getForLogin() returns createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel-wrapped models only on the delegate paths, while the cache-hit path returns raw cached models from session.identityProviders().getById(id), so the returned model type (and its organization-aware behavior, e.g. isEnabled) depends on whether the cache happened to be populated. The same call produces different results (wrapped vs raw model) depending on cache state; downstream callers like OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean are forced to defensively re-check isEnabled ('idp might have been wrapped'), and any consumer relying on the organization-aware wrapper gets divergent behavior between a cold and warm cache.

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider#getForLogin(), the cache-miss/invalid path returns models wrapped via .map(this::createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel), but the cache-hit path reconstructs results by IDs via session.identityProviders().getById(id) and returns identityProviders.stream() without applying createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel. From the diff alone, that means the method can return different model implementations/behavior depending on cache state, which is a correctness issue for callers expecting the organization-aware wrapper semantics.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] On the cache-hit path the cached ID set is materialized from a HashSet and returned via identityProviders.stream() with no ordering, whereas the delegate path returns the underlying store's ordered stream, so getForLogin() result ordering changes once the cache is populated. Callers that depend on the delegate's deterministic ordering (e.g. by display name via IDP_COMPARATOR in the login page bean, or any caller that doesn't re-sort) observe a different, nondeterministic order between first and subsequent requests — visible flickering/reordering of login-page IDP lists.

adjudication.rationale: In the new InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider#getForLogin cache-hit path, IDs are collected into a Set and then materialized into a `HashSet<IdentityProviderModel>` (`Set<IdentityProviderModel> identityProviders = new HashSet<>(); ... return identityProviders.stream();`). This loses any deterministic ordering that the delegate stream might have had. On the cache-miss path (`isInvalid(cacheKey)` or fallback), it directly returns `idpDelegate.getForLogin(...).map(...)`, preserving the delegate stream order. So the same query can return differently ordered results before vs. after caching, because `HashSet` iteration order is unspecified.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate decides invalidation solely by comparing the IDP's own model fields, but organization linkage is also mutated through the OrganizationProvider (addIdentityProvider/removeIdentityProvider), which never touches the IDP storage invalidation hooks, so login caches can go stale when org membership changes without a concurrent IDP update. The test only covers step 4 because the BROKER_PUBLIC config change happens to trigger the IDP-update path; an admin linking an already-public org-linked IDP to a different organization purely via the organization endpoint leaves the ORG_ONLY/ALL login caches serving the previous membership until some unrelated IDP write occurs.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds login-result caching keyed by realm+FetchMode and explicitly invalidates it on IDP create/update/remove. It also includes organizationId-aware invalidation on update (registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate invalidates when organizationId changes while the IDP remains eligible for login). The finding’s core claim—that org linkage mutations via OrganizationProvider “never” touch these invalidation hooks and therefore caches can go stale—is not verifiable from this diff. In fact, the added test’s step 4 expects the login caches to be cleared after calling organizations().identityProviders().addIdentityProvider(...), which implies there is some invalidation occurring on org-link changes (either via an IDP update of organizationId or other cache invalidation not shown), contradicting the assertion that org membership changes leave caches stale.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Every cleanup registration in testCacheIDPForLogin uses the literal alias 'idp-alias-' + i concatenated as a string for getCleanup().addCleanup(testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove), looking up a nonexistent IDP named 'alias', so none of the 22 created IDPs are actually removed after the test. The test leaks 22 identity providers into the shared test realm on every run; with a reused realm this pollutes subsequent login-cache count assertions (the assertEquals(5/6/10/11, ...) sizes) once another test's leftovers qualify as login IDPs, producing order-dependent failures.

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added `testCacheIDPForLogin` loop creating 20 IDPs, cleanup is registered as `getCleanup().addCleanup(testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove);` (and similarly after creating `idp-alias-20`). This looks up an IDP literally named "alias" rather than the created aliases (e.g., `"idp-alias-" + i` / `"idp-alias-20"`), so the created IDPs are not removed by the test cleanup. That can pollute the shared realm across runs and make subsequent count-based assertions order-dependent.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The new caller-side `idp.isEnabled()` re-check exists only in OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean, while every other consumer of getForLogin receives cached entries with no enabled re-check, making the login-eligibility enforcement caller-dependent rather than provider-enforced. Any current or future caller of getForLogin (e.g., broker login flows enumerating available identity providers) that does not duplicate this filter will render or act on an IdentityProviderModel whose enabled state was not revalidated against the cached set; the diff's own comment ('re-check isEnabled as idp might have been wrapped') documents that the cache/wrapping path can lose this state, so the guard lives at exactly one call site and is silently absent elsewhere.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows a new caller-side `idp.isEnabled()` filter added only in `OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean` (both branches of `searchForIdentityProviders`), justified by the inline comment that the IDP “might have been wrapped”. Meanwhile, the new `InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider.getForLogin(...)` caching path returns `IdentityProviderModel`s directly from `session.identityProviders().getById(id)` on cache hits and does not itself re-check `isEnabled()` at return time. From the diff alone it’s not provable that enabled-state can actually be lost/incorrect in the provider layer, but the change does make enabled filtering inconsistent and caller-dependent (at least for this caller), which is a concrete, diff-grounded design/consistency concern rather than a confirmed defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The cleanup registration inside the IDP-creation loop uses the hard-coded alias "alias" (testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove) instead of the created alias "idp-alias-" + i, so cleanup removes a non-existent provider and none of the 20+ created IDPs. Every run of testCacheIDPForLogin leaks ~21 identity providers and an organization membership set into the test realm; repeated executions (or other tests in the suite sharing the realm) see leftover IDPs that shift login-cache counts, making this test order-dependent and flaky, and the 'assertEquals(5/6/10/11)' counts silently depend on the leak never colliding with prior state.

adjudication.rationale: In testCacheIDPForLogin(), the IDP creation loop sets alias to "idp-alias-" + i but registers cleanup with a hard-coded lookup key: getCleanup().addCleanup(testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove);. This will not remove the created providers (unless an IDP literally named "alias" exists), so the test leaks the created IDPs into the realm and can make later assertions/order-dependent.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The test never asserts anything about the Stream<IdentityProviderModel> that getForLogin returns — every assertion inspects the internal IdentityProviderListQuery (cache bookkeeping) rather than the public contract. If getForLogin returned the wrong models (e.g., disabled IDPs leaking through, organization-aware wrapping applied incorrectly, or stale internalIds resolving to wrong providers), counts of internal ID sets could still match while the actual login page shows the wrong broker list; the cache-invalidation machinery is verified but the behavior the cache exists to serve is not.

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added test `testCacheIDPForLogin`, calls like `session.identityProviders().getForLogin(FetchMode.REALM_ONLY, null);` are never consumed/collected, and the assertions that follow only inspect `IdentityProviderListQuery` entries in the cache (e.g., `assertEquals(5, identityProviderListQuery.getIDPs("").size())`). The test therefore validates cache population/invalidation bookkeeping but does not assert the public behavior of `getForLogin` (which models are actually returned, enabled/disabled filtering, organization-aware wrapping). This is a concrete, diff-grounded gap in testing of the new caching path, not a functional defect in the production code itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Three new branches in InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider.getForLogin are never triggered by the test: the isInvalid(cacheKey) delegate fallback, the cached==null chained-query path (a second searchKey on an existing cache key), and the idp==null registerInvalidation-and-fall-back-to-delegate path. A regression in any of these paths — e.g., the chained-query constructor losing the previous search's entries, or the null-IDP fallback failing to register the invalidation so a deleted IDP's id stays cached — passes the suite; the null-IDP path in particular is the staleness safety net for concurrent removal and is completely unexercised.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds substantial branching logic in `InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider.getForLogin(...)`: (1) an early `if (isInvalid(cacheKey))` delegate fallback, (2) a `cached == null` path when a cache entry exists but the current `searchKey` (derived from `organizationId`) hasn’t been cached yet, and (3) an `idp == null` staleness-safety path that registers invalidation and falls back to the delegate. The new test `testCacheIDPForLogin` only calls `getForLogin` with one `searchKey` per `FetchMode` (`""` for `REALM_ONLY`, `orgaId` for `ORG_ONLY`/`ALL`), so it does not exercise the “second searchKey on existing cacheKey” (`cached == null`) branch. It also removes `idp-alias-1`, which is disabled in setup and therefore not part of the cached login IDPs, so it won’t trigger the `idp == null` fallback. Nothing in the test forces `isInvalid(cacheKey)` to be true at the time of `getForLogin` either. This is a concrete test gap for newly added nontrivial caching/staleness logic, not a proven functional defect in the diff itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The remove() code path's invalidating behavior is untested: the only removal in the test (idp-alias-1, disabled) exercises the no-op branch of registerIDPLoginInvalidation, never the case where removing a login-qualified IDP must invalidate all login caches. A regression that drops or breaks registerIDPLoginInvalidation(storedIdp) in remove() (including the newly added unconditional idpDelegate.getByAlias(alias) lookup that feeds it) leaves stale login caches after an admin deletes an active broker, and no test in this diff catches it.

adjudication.rationale: In the new `testCacheIDPForLogin`, the only removal is `idp-alias-1`, which (per setup `idpRep.setEnabled((i % 2) == 0)`) is disabled and thus does not qualify for login; therefore `registerIDPLoginInvalidation(storedIdp)` in `InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider.remove()` is exercised only in its no-op branch (`if (getLoginPredicate().test(idp)) { ... }`). The diff adds nontrivial behavior to invalidate all login caches on removal of a login-qualified IDP (and adds an unconditional `idpDelegate.getByAlias(alias)` lookup to feed that), but there is no test in this diff that would fail if a regression removed/broke that invalidation for an enabled/login-visible IDP.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The added idp.isEnabled() re-check on both filter branches (added to guard against wrapped disabled IDPs) has no test in this diff triggering it — the only test file modified is OrganizationCacheTest, which exercises the cache layer, not this bean. If the re-check is removed or inverted (or createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel stops preserving enabled=false), disabled brokers reappear on the organization login page and no test fails; the exact regression this defensive filter was added for is unverified.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new defensive filter in OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean.searchForIdentityProviders: `.filter(idp -> idp.isEnabled() && !Objects.equals(existingIDP, idp.getAlias()))` on both branches. The only test changes are in OrganizationCacheTest and they exercise the caching/invalidation behavior of `session.identityProviders().getForLogin(...)` and related cache keys, not the bean’s filtering logic or the rendered organization login page. So the newly added `isEnabled()` re-check is not directly verified by any test in this diff; removing/inverting it would not obviously break the added/modified tests here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate only compares getOrganizationId() for the both-qualify case, so toggling OrganizationModel.BROKER_PUBLIC on an organization-linked IDP changes the login predicate result but skips login-cache invalidation entirely. An admin who removes BROKER_PUBLIC from an org-linked broker (making it non-login per the new predicate clause in IdentityProviderStorageProvider.java:254) gets no invalidation; all FetchMode caches keep serving the IDP's internalId, the login page keeps offering the broker until the entry expires or an unrelated write invalidates it — stale login options reported as fresh.

adjudication.rationale: In registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate, login-cache invalidation is skipped only when (a) both original and updated do NOT satisfy getLoginPredicate(), or (b) both satisfy getLoginPredicate() and the organizationId is unchanged. If an org-linked IDP has BROKER_PUBLIC toggled off, the new getLoginPredicate() clause (orgId != null requires BROKER_PUBLIC=true) makes the predicate change from true->false, so neither early-return applies and the method falls through to invalidate all FetchMode login caches. Thus the described “predicate changes but invalidation is skipped entirely” does not match the diff’s control flow.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The cache-hit path of getForLogin returns raw models from session.identityProviders().getById(id) while the miss/fallback paths wrap every model with createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel, so the same query returns structurally different results depending on cache warmth. On a cold cache the caller gets organization-aware wrappers (whose isEnabled/behavior differs, which is exactly why OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean.java:75/81 had to add an isEnabled re-check 'as idp might have been wrapped'), but on a warm cache it gets plain models — the wrapper-dependent behavior silently diverges between the two paths, producing nondeterministic login-page broker lists depending on which node/path populated the cache.

adjudication.rationale: In `InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider#getForLogin`, the cache-miss path returns `idpDelegate.getForLogin(...).map(this::createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel)` (wrapped models), but the cache-hit path reconstructs results via `session.identityProviders().getById(id)` and returns them directly without applying `createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel`. This makes the returned `IdentityProviderModel` instances structurally/behaviorally different depending on whether the login list was cached, matching the finding’s nondeterminism concern.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] remove() now unconditionally calls idpDelegate.getByAlias(alias) (a real store read) before checking the cache, where previously the delegate lookup only happened on the isInvalid(cacheKey) path. Every remove() of an IDP — including removes of IDPs that were never login-eligible, where the fetched model is only used to decide an invalidation that never fires — now pays an extra DB round-trip; the caching layer it lives in is bypassed on this read with no benefit in the common non-login case.

adjudication.rationale: Diff shows `remove(String alias)` now does `IdentityProviderModel storedIdp = idpDelegate.getByAlias(alias);` unconditionally before the `isInvalid(cacheKey)` check. Previously, the delegate lookup was only done on the `isInvalid(cacheKey)` path (`registerIDPInvalidation(idpDelegate.getByAlias(alias))`). Since `storedIdp` is mainly used for `registerIDPLoginInvalidation(storedIdp)` and for invalidation when cache is invalid, this introduces an extra underlying-store read on every remove, even when login-cache invalidation won’t apply. This is a concrete performance/regression concern, not a correctness bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] registerIDPLoginInvalidation is called in create() and remove() with the pre-persist/pre-removed model and relies entirely on getLoginPredicate(); for remove() of a login-eligible IDP the predicate is evaluated on a model object the caller may have mutated or that no longer reflects stored state, while create() invalidates before the delegate write completes. Invalidation correctness is coupled to the caller-supplied model rather than stored state — a caller that constructs a create/update model without enabled/org fields populated (e.g. partial update payloads where unset config fields come back null) gets the wrong invalidation decision and stale or needlessly-cleared login caches; next writer of a new create/remove call site inherits this trap.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows remove() now fetches the stored model via `IdentityProviderModel storedIdp = idpDelegate.getByAlias(alias);` and passes that to `registerIDPLoginInvalidation(storedIdp)`, so the predicate is evaluated on delegate-loaded state, not a caller-mutated/pre-removed object. For create(), invalidation is done on the same `model` that is then persisted by `idpDelegate.create(model)`; the claim about “partial update payloads” doesn’t match create/remove semantics shown here, and there’s no evidence in the diff that create models are incomplete or that invalidation-before-write causes incorrect cache behavior.
